dissertation: Schwabe,I.(2016). Nature,Nurture and Item Response Theory: A Psychometric Approach to Behaviour Genetics. PhD dissertation,University of Twente. https://doi.org/10.3990/1.9789036540735 164-page2016 doctoral dissertation; original thesis chapters include one published article, two in-press chapters, one under-revision chapter and one manuscript-in-preparation, not later article revisions. Degree: Doctor, University of Twente; defended 2016-03-24; ISBN 978-90-365-4073-5.
synthesis: We partially replicated Schwabe (2016). In the reconstructed Chapter6 primary grid, all108 deletion-minus-full variance-SE contrasts favor full information and all108 multiplicity-adjusted intervals exclude zero positively. MAR deletion-bias directions agree in all36 component-condition cells, while full-information zero bias is not established by nonsignificant intervals. All216 literal plotted variance-SE values differ outside conditional comparison bands; original SE implementation and source Monte Carlo uncertainty remain unresolved, and exploratory path-SE agreement cannot substitute for variance SE. The completed96000method fits include72000primary and24000sensitivity fits. Narrow analytical and software semantics are verified under their stated assumptions. Independent empirical refits and full Bayesian recovery/power grids remain unestablished or blocked. A four-chain one-dataset Bayesian diagnostic completed but failed its joint convergence gate. Whole-dissertation replication is not complete. Additional completed evidence comprises 2650 response-generation datasets across 19 conditions, paired raw-versus-standardized alpha sensitivity on the same datasets, 21 completed descriptive assessments among 26 saved Chapter 6 targets, with five direct-power or unequal-structure targets still pending, and conditional ordinary mathematical derivations. These do not establish missing power, source-count posterior recovery, original empirical refits, or a unique finite likelihood maximum. The completed centered four-chain 12000-retained-draw diagnostic also fails its unchanged joint gate; the final recovery outcome is not incorporated.
limitations: Historical one-dataset posterior runs and short pilots do not reproduce the source100-dataset Chapter2 or250-dataset Chapter5 summaries; convergence and repeated-dataset uncertainty remain unestablished.
Unavailable original empirical responses, calibration/linkage records, joint posterior draws and underreported designs prevent the corresponding independent empirical or exact-design comparisons.
Figure geometry and arithmetic from printed parameters reuse source evidence; they do not reproduce original data generation or empirical fits.
Conditional ordinary mathematical arguments do not supply formal certification or verify empirical calibration, observation and support assumptions.

H6.precision-grid:36primary conditions and12additional3%missingness sensitivity conditions are distinct; low-missingness source2%prose/3%plot ambiguity remains. Source-derived geometric bounds are neither original Monte Carlo uncertainty nor equivalence margins.

C6-3.MAR-bias.A,C6-3.MAR-bias.C,C6-3.MAR-bias.h2:11point sign reversals occur under full information; none excludes zero after adjustment. Both conditional MAR source-estimate deviations occur at ambiguous low missingness.

H2.IRT-bias-remedy,H2.power-grid and Chapter5 Bayesian claims:the bounded four-chain one-dataset diagnostic fails its joint convergence gate. No source100/250dataset aggregate, power fraction or empirical effect is inferred from it.
C1.scale-invariance and Chapter5/6 analytical claims:ordinary arguments are assumption-bound and not Lean-certified. Population identification is not finite-sample likelihood uniqueness.
Whole-dissertation inventory:996linked records include shared components, source-only arithmetic and parents; they are not996independent findings and no replication success fraction is defined.

C2-2.design.alpha, C2-3.alpha, C5-2.alpha.J60 and C5-2.alpha.J20: source alpha formula/aggregation/calibration remain ambiguous; rounding of reconstructed means is not an exact source-estimand verdict. Standardization does not close the floor/ceiling or J20 descriptor gaps.

C6-2.SE-trend.MCAR.A and other saved-target assessments: qualitative constancy, slightness, closeness and adequacy lack justified equivalence margins. Descriptive trends cannot settle those qualifications or H6.power-assertion.

C5-1.logvariance-identification and C2-1.construction: conditional ordinary proofs do not establish finite-sample maximum existence/uniqueness or observed-response identification of non-Gaussian latent moments.
H2.power-grid and H2.IRT-bias-remedy: a failed centered one-dataset joint gate cannot supply source-count recovery or power; final recovery result is withheld pending terminal review.

ours.value: For Y~Bernoulli(p(theta)), p=logistic(a*(theta-b)), the theta score is a*(Y-p). Thus Fisher information for theta is E[score^2]=a^2*p*(1-p), also equal to minus expected second derivative. The crop confirms Eq3.4 actually prints p*(1-p), without a^2. At a=2,theta=b, true theta information is1, whereas the printed expression is1/4. Existing finite-difference output 0.9999999999131821 independently corroborates this exact discrepancy. For unit positive slope a=1, Eq3.4 is correct. It also equals information for each item-specific logit coordinate eta=a*(theta-b), but those differently scaled coordinates cannot be treated as a single common theta without Jacobian factors. Under fixed known calibration and conditional item independence, the likelihood factors and the total theta score is the sum of independent mean-zero item scores. Its variance equals the sum of the correct item information values, establishing Eq3.5. TI(theta)^(-1/2) is the conventional information-based conditional standard-error function for TI>0. If interpreted as an exact finite-sample sampling SD or an arbitrary posterior SD, Eq3.6 is not generally established: equality with actual estimator variance requires efficiency/appropriate approximation, and posterior uncertainty depends on the prior.

ours.value: AppendixB defines eta_k=alpha*(theta-beta_k), s_k=sum_{l=1}^k eta_l, and p_k=exp(s_k)/sum_{j=1}^3 exp(s_j). For finite real inputs each term is positive, the denominator is positive, and sum_k p_k=1 exactly. For k=2,3, log(p_k/p_{k-1})=s_k-s_{k-1}=alpha*(theta-beta_k). Thus adjacent-category logits agree with the implemented cumulative-exponential model. The common eta_1 factor cancels from all probabilities: after cancellation weights are 1, exp(eta_2), exp(eta_2+eta_3). beta_1 fixed at0 is a redundant reference contribution, with effective transitions at beta_2,beta_3. The inspected crop instead prints p_no=1/(1+u*v), p_question=p_no*u, p_yes=p_no*p_question*v, with u=exp(alpha*(theta-beta_1)), v=exp(alpha*(theta-beta_2)). At theta=0 and both displayed thresholds0, alpha=1, these probabilities are1/2,1/2,1/4, summing to5/4. The discrepancy is in the source ink, not merely text extraction. At that zero setting, the AppendixB cumulative-exponential model gives three probabilities1/3. Its indexing uses beta_2,beta_3 as transitions; one cannot silently identify these with the literal printed beta_1,beta_2 expressions without explaining the remapping.

claims.methods: The source free-common-mean assumption is confirmed by the saved independent source audit: mu is a fitted parameter; setting mu=0 in data generation is not a fitted constraint. The existing all-zero-response argument shows likelihood strictly improves as free mu decreases and tends to supremum1 without attainment. It is a valid counterexample to universal existence of a finite MLE, including when both zygosities and both moderator levels are represented. The example does not produce two local or global maxima. ours.value: Let x=(x1,x2) have covariance [[S,B],[B,S]], S=W+B, and yj=mu+beta^T*xj+uj. The residual pair u is independent of x with variance A+C+E and covariance rho*A+C. Then Var(yj)=A+C+E+beta^T*S*beta, Cov(y1,y2)=rho*A+C+beta^T*B*beta, Cov(yj,xj)=beta^T*S and Cov(yj,x_other)=beta^T*B. These are all blocks of Eq6.5. Equivalently transform the block-diagonal covariance of (u,x) by the linear map (u,x)->(y,x).

ours.value: Partition a jointly Gaussian vector into missing U and observed O with fixed known mean/covariance and nonsingular Sigma_OO. E[U|O]=mu_U+Sigma_UO*Sigma_OO^{-1}*(O-mu_O), and Var(U|O)=Sigma_UU-Sigma_UO*Sigma_OO^{-1}*Sigma_OU. The removed quadratic form is positive semidefinite. Additional observed variables reduce conditional variance further by their residual covariance with U after conditioning on current O. Strict reduction requires nonzero conditional covariance; marginal correlation alone does not ensure incremental information after other observations. The conditional mean depends on correlated observed values, so a co-twin covariate and phenotypes can inform a missing value. Exact scalar-covariate illustration: W=B=1,beta=1/2, residual A=1/2,C=3/10,E=1/5,rho=1/2. With missing x1, successive conditional variances after observing nothing,x2,(x2,y1),(x2,y1,y2) are2,3/2,12/11,279/286. Every decrease is exact and strict.

The original simulation driver, exact beta allocation, fitting/plotting SE implementation and source Monte Carlo error are unavailable; equal covariate coefficients are a declared reconstruction assumption.

Passing numerical guards does not certify a global optimum or correct missingness/latent-model assumptions. No source equivalence or direct power result follows.
Parent/component claims reuse the same simulations; claims are not independent replication counts.

ours.value: Given Gaussian liability L and threshold t=0, define V=1{L>=0}. The script draws X|L as Bernoulli(epsilon+(1-2*epsilon)*V), epsilon=0.001. Thus probabilities are0.001 below threshold and0.999 at/above threshold; this is not a deterministic threshold observation. For L~Normal(mu,sigma^2),sigma>0, P(X=1)=0.001+0.998*Phi(mu/sigma). At mu0 this equals1/2. Conditionally independent observation errors imply Cov(X1,X2)=0.998^2*Cov(V1,V2). Conditional Bernoulli variance is0.001*0.999, not0. Conditional on fixed hyperparameters gamma_cov and the zygosity-specific precision matrices, the Gaussian hierarchy has shared family psi and independent within-twin innovations. Thus its latent covariance blocks are B_z+W_z on the diagonal and B_z across twins, where B_z=tau_b_z inverse and W_z=tau_w_z inverse, separately for MZ and DZ. The source uses separate MZ/DZ Wishart precision distributions. This is not a claim of a common B/W or a Gaussian marginal after integrating over their priors. Observed binary X variables are non-Gaussian.

claims.statement: Full information gives lower variance-component standard errors than deletion across the investigated missingness mechanisms and design grid.
claims.level_rationale: The source presents a common precision pattern over mechanisms and variance components, not nine separately motivated scientific conclusions. Source emphasis: Chapter6 results pp93–95; discussion p101.

published.unavailable_reason: There is no single scalar precision gain across three mechanisms, three variance components, four covariate counts and three missingness levels. All108 signed deletion-minus-full-information contrasts are retained; none is an aggregate.

claims.source_uncertainty: Retain all component-specific source uncertainty and missing uncertainty; a qualitative conjunction has no invented pooled standard error.
claims.source_multiplicity: Components share datasets, calibrations, posterior simulations and design assumptions. They are not independent replications; no success fraction over inventory records is meaningful.
limitations: There is no single scalar precision gain across three mechanisms, three variance components, four covariate counts and three missingness levels. All108 signed deletion-minus-full-information contrasts are retained; none is an aggregate.
Source-only hierarchy independent of our outcomes. No combined source effect or success verdict is inferred.

The original simulation driver, exact beta allocation, fitting/plotting SE implementation and source Monte Carlo error are unavailable; equal covariate coefficients are a declared reconstruction assumption.
The source methods/captions say2% while plotted low-missing curves say3%; primary2% and sensitivity3% results remain separate.
Passing numerical guards does not certify a global optimum or correct missingness/latent-model assumptions. No source equivalence or direct power result follows.
Parent/component claims reuse the same simulations; claims are not independent replication counts.
claims.source_finding: Full information gives lower variance-component standard errors than deletion across the investigated missingness mechanisms and design grid.
claims.dependency_notice: Inventory records are not independent scientific findings or replications. Use source conditions and shared simulation, posterior, dataset, calibration and model dependencies; do not compute a success fraction over records.
claims.applicability_reason: The principal precision conclusion spans108 signed SE contrasts across three mechanisms, three variance components, four covariate counts and three missingness levels. All108 parent contrasts and their existing extraction bounds remain; no pooled precision gain is invented.

current_coverage.supporting_evidence_scope: For Y~Bernoulli(p(theta)), p=logistic(a*(theta-b)), the theta score is a*(Y-p). Thus Fisher information for theta is E[score^2]=a^2*p*(1-p), also equal to minus expected second derivative. The crop confirms Eq3.4 actually prints p*(1-p), without a^2. At a=2,theta=b, true theta information is1, whereas the printed expression is1/4. Existing finite-difference output 0.9999999999131821 independently corroborates this exact discrepancy. For unit positive slope a=1, Eq3.4 is correct. It also equals information for each item-specific logit coordinate eta=a*(theta-b), but those differently scaled coordinates cannot be treated as a single common theta without Jacobian factors. Under fixed known calibration and conditional item independence, the likelihood factors and the total theta score is the sum of independent mean-zero item scores. Its variance equals the sum of the correct item information values, establishing Eq3.5. TI(theta)^(-1/2) is the conventional information-based conditional standard-error function for TI>0. If interpreted as an exact finite-sample sampling SD or an arbitrary posterior SD, Eq3.6 is not generally established: equality with actual estimator variance requires efficiency/appropriate approximation, and posterior uncertainty depends on the prior.

current_coverage.supporting_evidence_scope: AppendixB defines eta_k=alpha*(theta-beta_k), s_k=sum_{l=1}^k eta_l, and p_k=exp(s_k)/sum_{j=1}^3 exp(s_j). For finite real inputs each term is positive, the denominator is positive, and sum_k p_k=1 exactly. For k=2,3, log(p_k/p_{k-1})=s_k-s_{k-1}=alpha*(theta-beta_k). Thus adjacent-category logits agree with the implemented cumulative-exponential model. The common eta_1 factor cancels from all probabilities: after cancellation weights are 1, exp(eta_2), exp(eta_2+eta_3). beta_1 fixed at0 is a redundant reference contribution, with effective transitions at beta_2,beta_3. The inspected crop instead prints p_no=1/(1+u*v), p_question=p_no*u, p_yes=p_no*p_question*v, with u=exp(alpha*(theta-beta_1)), v=exp(alpha*(theta-beta_2)). At theta=0 and both displayed thresholds0, alpha=1, these probabilities are1/2,1/2,1/4, summing to5/4. The discrepancy is in the source ink, not merely text extraction. At that zero setting, the AppendixB cumulative-exponential model gives three probabilities1/3. Its indexing uses beta_2,beta_3 as transitions; one cannot silently identify these with the literal printed beta_1,beta_2 expressions without explaining the remapping.

current_coverage.attempted_evidence: Partition a jointly Gaussian vector into missing U and observed O with fixed known mean/covariance and nonsingular Sigma_OO. E[U|O]=mu_U+Sigma_UO*Sigma_OO^{-1}*(O-mu_O), and Var(U|O)=Sigma_UU-Sigma_UO*Sigma_OO^{-1}*Sigma_OU. The removed quadratic form is positive semidefinite. Additional observed variables reduce conditional variance further by their residual covariance with U after conditioning on current O. Strict reduction requires nonzero conditional covariance; marginal correlation alone does not ensure incremental information after other observations. The conditional mean depends on correlated observed values, so a co-twin covariate and phenotypes can inform a missing value. Exact scalar-covariate illustration: W=B=1,beta=1/2, residual A=1/2,C=3/10,E=1/5,rho=1/2. With missing x1, successive conditional variances after observing nothing,x2,(x2,y1),(x2,y1,y2) are2,3/2,12/11,279/286. Every decrease is exact and strict.

claims.proposed_adjudication: Established by ordinary exact analytical replication under the explicit shared-binary-moderator assumptions; no substantive remaining algebraic obligation for this narrow target.
claims.source_reading: The appendix first gives simultaneous global sign symmetry, then shows that requiring the baseline genetic path positive still permits two moderation slopes at binary moderator endpoints.
claims.argument: For path a+b*m with a>0 and shared m in{0,1}, bstar=-2*a-b leaves a fixed and maps the other endpoint a+b to -(a+b). Squared paths, component variances and within-pair covariance contributions are unchanged. With independent Gaussian ACE components, equal means and residual structure, the complete observed Gaussian phenotype distribution is unchanged, and so is its probability after the same measurement kernel. Existing symbolic difference -4*a*m*(a+b)*(m-1) vanishes at both endpoints.
assumptions_limits: Distinct alternative slopes require a+b!=0; a zero endpoint coalesces the two roots. The source wording of always two distinct combinations needs this ordinary degeneracy qualification.
No path-positivity constraint at both endpoints; adding that extra constraint would eliminate the reflected endpoint.
Shared moderator is essential to this endpoint argument; arbitrary separate-twin moderator cross-products are not covered.
Identical likelihood parameterizations do not ensure a maximizer exists for every finite dataset. If an optimum with nonzero endpoints exists, its reflected unrestricted point shares its likelihood.
claims.remaining: No new empirical data or numerical fit is required to verify this symmetry. Formal certification is separate.

claims.proposed_adjudication: Established for the source global-sign nonidentification extension on unrestricted paths; positive-baseline residual nonidentification does not extend from binary to rich continuous support. Keep these readings separate rather than mark the whole algebra unresolved.
source_locators: AppendixC pp138-139 global-sign argument and positive-baseline paragraph
claims.source_reading: The final sentence says the proof extends to ACE models and continuous covariates, without restating whether positive-baseline restrictions are imposed. The preceding text contains both global symmetry and the stronger binary positive-baseline claim.
claims.argument: Unrestricted (a,b) and(-a,-b) yield exactly the same squared path for every real m; simultaneously changing both twin loadings also preserves their products. Each independent ACE component has this global sign symmetry. Conversely if squared affine paths agree at three distinct moderator values, their degree-at-most-two difference is identically zero. Factoring it implies the paths are identical or globally negative. With strictly positive intercepts only the identical solution remains. Existing exact midpoint witness 9/25 versus1/100 shows the binary reflection generally fails between endpoints.
assumptions_limits: Three distinct support values suffice for the path polynomial result; continuous support supplies them. Equality of component variance functions is assumed/identified before invoking this algebra.
If a=0, a nonnegative rather than strictly positive convention may leave a slope sign ambiguity.
The polynomial argument is not an assertion of full observed-item model likelihood unimodality.
claims.remaining: Source interpretation should be qualified explicitly: unrestricted global symmetry replicated; any stronger reading retaining the positive-baseline binary ambiguity on continuous support is not supported and is contradicted at the variance-function level under the stated support and sign convention.

claims.proposed_adjudication: Established by exact derivative; narrow target fully addressed by ordinary analysis.
claims.argument: For V(m)=exp(beta0+beta1*m), Vprime=beta1*exp(beta0+beta1*m). It is strictly increasing for beta1>0, strictly decreasing for beta1<0 and constant for beta1=0. A squared affine path has derivative 2*b*(a+b*m), which changes sign at its vertex when that vertex is inside the moderator domain.
assumptions_limits: Finite real coefficients and real moderator. Constant zero-slope case is included in weak monotonicity.
A squared-affine curve can itself be monotone on a restricted moderator domain; the comparison does not say every observed squared-path curve turns.
Variance-curve monotonicity says nothing about concavity or uniqueness of a likelihood maximum.
claims.remaining: None for the elementary variance-curve property; no simulation or formal proof assistant needed to consider this replication attempted and established.

claims.proposed_adjudication: Established by ordinary hierarchical variance/covariance calculation for the specified shared-moderator Gaussian model. Do not conflate this narrow target with the separate full observed-item identification claim.
argument: Fix M=m and abbreviate exp(beta0a+beta1a*m)=A, similarly C,E. Under the stated independent innovations, MZ traits equal mu+beta1m*m+U_C+U_A+U_Ej, with innovation variances C,A,E. Hence both means are mu+beta1m*m, both variances T=A+C+E, and covariance K_MZ=A+C.

For DZ, Eq5.12 gives a shared genetic innovation of variance1/2 and Eq5.13 adds an independent individual innovation of variance1/2. Multiplying by sqrt(A) in Eq5.14 gives each genetic variance A and cross-twin genetic covariance A/2. Adding the common C and independent E innovations yields the same mean and T, and K_DZ=A/2+C.
This also verifies the inverse identities A=2*(K_MZ-K_DZ), C=2*K_DZ-K_MZ, E=T-K_MZ already independently symbolically checked.
assumptions_limits: Shared moderator, common component functions across zygosity, independent family/component/individual innovations as specified by the hierarchy; genetic correlation1 or1/2.
Correct square-root scaling in Eq5.14 matters: text extraction separates its radical; the prose explicitly describes scaling by the standard deviation.
These are model-implied moments, not a claim that observed empirical responses satisfy the model or that a sampler converged.
claims.remaining: No outstanding substantive calculation for the narrow moment target. Estimation, empirical validity and full observation-model identification are separate targets.

claims.proposed_adjudication: Partially addressed; finite-sample at-most-one-maximum claim remains unresolved. Do not label it disproved solely by a no-finite-maximum example, and do not infer it from population injectivity.

claims.source_reading: The exact source wording asserts only one maximum in the likelihood function. It links this to identification, but does not explicitly quantify existence of a finite optimum for every possible dataset. The stronger universal existence reading is our interpretation and must be labeled accordingly.
established: The source free-common-mean assumption is confirmed by the saved independent source audit: mu is a fitted parameter; setting mu=0 in data generation is not a fitted constraint.

The existing all-zero-response argument shows likelihood strictly improves as free mu decreases and tends to supremum1 without attainment. It is a valid counterexample to universal existence of a finite MLE, including when both zygosities and both moderator levels are represented.
The example does not produce two local or global maxima. If only one maximum is read as at most one when one exists, no counterexample to that claim has been supplied.

The independently reviewed joint-item argument establishes population parameter injectivity under known finite positive logistic calibrations, two distinct conditionally independent observations, positive Gaussian ACE components, observed moments and joint zygosity/moderator support. Together with correct specification this yields a unique population expected-log-likelihood maximizer via KL divergence. It does not yield finite-likelihood concavity or global uniqueness.
genuinely_remaining: Proof or counterexample for at-most-one finite local/global likelihood maximum under a precisely specified nondegenerate observation design and parameter constraints. Neither existing sign-symmetry removal nor monotone variance curves proves it.
Verification of actual source empirical calibration, missingness, support and model assumptions remains separate; no empirical likelihood landscape was certified.
A proper prior changes the objective; no conclusion about posterior unimodality, propriety or MCMC convergence follows from the all-zero likelihood example.
claims.recommended_report: Population identification conditionally established; universal finite-MLE existence fails for possible all-zero data with free mean; uniqueness of a finite maximum when one exists remains unresolved. This qualifies the source wording without silently strengthening it.

claims.proposed_status: Established ordinary analytical identity under stated Gaussian regression assumptions.
claims.source_locator: Chapter6 pp88-89 Eqs6.1-6.5; AppendixF covariance construction; local original full_information_approach.R covariance definitions
claims.derivation: Let x=(x1,x2) have covariance [[S,B],[B,S]], S=W+B, and yj=mu+beta^T*xj+uj. The residual pair u is independent of x with variance A+C+E and covariance rho*A+C. Then Var(yj)=A+C+E+beta^T*S*beta, Cov(y1,y2)=rho*A+C+beta^T*B*beta, Cov(yj,xj)=beta^T*S and Cov(yj,x_other)=beta^T*B. These are all blocks of Eq6.5. Equivalently transform the block-diagonal covariance of (u,x) by the linear map (u,x)->(y,x).
claims.assumptions: Symmetric valid W,B, common beta and covariate covariance across twins, residual independence from covariates, rho1 or1/2. Positive definiteness is needed for subsequent nonsingular conditional formulas.
claims.checks: Our exact-arithmetic check checks the linear-map construction against the separately assembled displayed blocks for q=1..5 and both zygosities, using nonconstant rational beta. All ten match exactly. Existing outputs/analytic-checks.json q2..5 checks the source simulation design numerically, including explained fraction0.64/1.64 and DZ cross-covariance.
claims.uncertainty: MCSE, confidence intervals and source rounding tolerance are inapplicable to this exact identity. Existing floating-point discrepancies are arithmetic precision, not sampling error. The source narrative39% is a rounded description of0.64/1.64, separate from covariance identity.

claims.source_locator: Chapter6 pp90-91 Section6.1.3; covariance assumptions pp88-89
derivation: Partition a jointly Gaussian vector into missing U and observed O with fixed known mean/covariance and nonsingular Sigma_OO. E[U|O]=mu_U+Sigma_UO*Sigma_OO^{-1}*(O-mu_O), and Var(U|O)=Sigma_UU-Sigma_UO*Sigma_OO^{-1}*Sigma_OU. The removed quadratic form is positive semidefinite. Additional observed variables reduce conditional variance further by their residual covariance with U after conditioning on current O.

Strict reduction requires nonzero conditional covariance; marginal correlation alone does not ensure incremental information after other observations. The conditional mean depends on correlated observed values, so a co-twin covariate and phenotypes can inform a missing value.

Exact scalar-covariate illustration: W=B=1,beta=1/2, residual A=1/2,C=3/10,E=1/5,rho=1/2. With missing x1, successive conditional variances after observing nothing,x2,(x2,y1),(x2,y1,y2) are2,3/2,12/11,279/286. Every decrease is exact and strict.
limits: Conditional uncertainty for a missing value with known parameters is different from a fitted biometric parameter SE with nuisance parameters estimated. No guarantee of lower SE in every realized finite fit is asserted.

The Gaussian prediction statement requires correct joint specification and suitable handling of the observation mechanism. Informative missingness not captured by the likelihood can invalidate inference.
No direct power experiment, universal missingness-scenario comparison, or observed empirical improvement is supplied by this small example.
claims.uncertainty: No Monte Carlo sampling; MCSE and printed rounding verdicts are inapplicable.

derivation: Given Gaussian liability L and threshold t=0, define V=1{L>=0}. The script draws X|L as Bernoulli(epsilon+(1-2*epsilon)*V), epsilon=0.001. Thus probabilities are0.001 below threshold and0.999 at/above threshold; this is not a deterministic threshold observation.

For L~Normal(mu,sigma^2),sigma>0, P(X=1)=0.001+0.998*Phi(mu/sigma). At mu0 this equals1/2. Conditionally independent observation errors imply Cov(X1,X2)=0.998^2*Cov(V1,V2). Conditional Bernoulli variance is0.001*0.999, not0.

Conditional on fixed hyperparameters gamma_cov and the zygosity-specific precision matrices, the Gaussian hierarchy has shared family psi and independent within-twin innovations. Thus its latent covariance blocks are B_z+W_z on the diagonal and B_z across twins, where B_z=tau_b_z inverse and W_z=tau_w_z inverse, separately for MZ and DZ. The source uses separate MZ/DZ Wishart precision distributions. This is not a claim of a common B/W or a Gaussian marginal after integrating over their priors. Observed binary X variables are non-Gaussian.

claims.argument: Let V_A>0 denote the genetic variance, s_A=sqrt(V_A), and v_E(g)=exp(beta0+beta1*g). Then v_E(g+s_A)/v_E(g)=exp(beta1*s_A)=Delta>0 for any g. Taking logarithms uniquely gives beta1=log(Delta)/s_A. In particular the source comparison uses g=0 and g=s_A; its baseline environmental variance is exp(beta0), not beta0 itself.

claims.locator: Chapter3 p36 Eq3.3 and p37 Eqs3.4-3.6; inspected evidence/eq3-information.png
claims.proposed_status: Analytical audit completed with a literal formula discrepancy: Eq3.4 is correct for unit slope, but not for general source OPLM slopes. Additivity and inverse-information uncertainty require their stated interpretation.
argument: For Y~Bernoulli(p(theta)), p=logistic(a*(theta-b)), the theta score is a*(Y-p). Thus Fisher information for theta is E[score^2]=a^2*p*(1-p), also equal to minus expected second derivative.

The crop confirms Eq3.4 actually prints p*(1-p), without a^2. At a=2,theta=b, true theta information is1, whereas the printed expression is1/4. Existing finite-difference output 0.9999999999131821 independently corroborates this exact discrepancy.

For unit positive slope a=1, Eq3.4 is correct. It also equals information for each item-specific logit coordinate eta=a*(theta-b), but those differently scaled coordinates cannot be treated as a single common theta without Jacobian factors.

Under fixed known calibration and conditional item independence, the likelihood factors and the total theta score is the sum of independent mean-zero item scores. Its variance equals the sum of the correct item information values, establishing Eq3.5.

TI(theta)^(-1/2) is the conventional information-based conditional standard-error function for TI>0. If interpreted as an exact finite-sample sampling SD or an arbitrary posterior SD, Eq3.6 is not generally established: equality with actual estimator variance requires efficiency/appropriate approximation, and posterior uncertainty depends on the prior.
limits: No missing discrimination factor can be excused merely because the OPLM slopes are treated as known; their derivatives with respect to theta still enter information.
Actual Figure3.2 computations/calibration files were not obtained. A printed error does not establish that its plotted implementation omitted a^2.
Information additivity and normalization of SE cannot validate the source empirical biometric conclusions.
claims.remaining: Actual plotted implementation remains unresolved; no additional algebra or model run is needed to establish the printed unit-slope versus OPLM distinction.

argument: AppendixB defines eta_k=alpha*(theta-beta_k), s_k=sum_{l=1}^k eta_l, and p_k=exp(s_k)/sum_{j=1}^3 exp(s_j). For finite real inputs each term is positive, the denominator is positive, and sum_k p_k=1 exactly.

For k=2,3, log(p_k/p_{k-1})=s_k-s_{k-1}=alpha*(theta-beta_k). Thus adjacent-category logits agree with the implemented cumulative-exponential model. The common eta_1 factor cancels from all probabilities: after cancellation weights are 1, exp(eta_2), exp(eta_2+eta_3). beta_1 fixed at0 is a redundant reference contribution, with effective transitions at beta_2,beta_3.

The inspected crop instead prints p_no=1/(1+u*v), p_question=p_no*u, p_yes=p_no*p_question*v, with u=exp(alpha*(theta-beta_1)), v=exp(alpha*(theta-beta_2)). At theta=0 and both displayed thresholds0, alpha=1, these probabilities are1/2,1/2,1/4, summing to5/4. The discrepancy is in the source ink, not merely text extraction.

At that zero setting, the AppendixB cumulative-exponential model gives three probabilities1/3. Its indexing uses beta_2,beta_3 as transitions; one cannot silently identify these with the literal printed beta_1,beta_2 expressions without explaining the remapping.

limits: This certifies the mathematical probability kernel specified by the printed AppendixB code, not that empirical fits ran that exact source version or converged.

restricted_population_statement.statement: Any two prespecified subsets satisfying the conditions below identify the same true latent Gaussian ACE parameter at each supported observed moderator value, and hence the same heritability and log-variance moderator coefficients, on the common anchored scale.
hypotheses: One correctly specified common scalar latent Gaussian twin ACE model, with finite mean and strictly positive A(M), C(M), E(M); independent families; M is a shared observed family moderator. Conditional latent means and total variances agree across zygosity; genetic correlations are 1 for MZ and 1/2 for DZ.

Each retained subset contains at least two distinct binary item observations conditionally independent given the latent trait, with known finite strictly positive logistic slopes and known finite intercepts on the SAME fixed common scale. The two item calibrations may coincide, but the binary observations must be distinct. Cross-twin measurement errors are conditionally independent.

Each subset supplies identifiable population within-person marginal and joint probabilities and cross-twin joint probabilities. These must be observable under the administration/missingness/selection scheme, or separately justified; item calibration alone does not identify missing joint moments.

Both MZ and DZ have positive joint support at EACH of two distinct moderator levels. For the coefficient conclusion, means are linear and positive ACE variances log-linear in the moderator. No change of population, ascertainment or moderator coding between subsets.

Subsets are fixed independently of the realized responses for the population sampling statement, or an appropriate observation/selection model is correctly included. These are sufficient added mathematical hypotheses, not an assertion that the source verified them in every application.
derivation: Let eta0 be the true common model parameter and P_eta^S the marginal response distribution for subset S. Correct specification and marginalization give P_true^S=P_eta0^S for every admissible S.

The previously independently reviewed joint-item argument identifies (mu,sqrt(T)) from p=E f(theta) and q=E[f(theta)g(theta)] for two calibrated positive-slope conditionally independent observations. Relabel so f has the larger slope. The fixed-p curve has strictly increasing q in s>0. This argument permits equal item calibration.

With mu,T fixed, a cross-twin item joint probability is strictly increasing in interior Gaussian covariance K, since its derivative is E[fprime(theta1)gprime(theta2)]>0. Thus both K_MZ and K_DZ are identified.
Recover A=2(K_MZ-K_DZ), C=2*K_DZ-K_MZ, E=T-K_MZ at each supported moderator value. Two moderator values identify the stated log-linear component and linear mean coefficients.

Consequently P_eta^S=P_eta0^S implies eta=eta0 for every admissible subset separately. Hence subsets share the population parameter and any fixed function of it, including A/T and the measured-moderator log-variance slopes. This is a corollary of existing conditional identification, not a new general theorem about all IRT models.

Equivalently, at two supported moderator values, the population expected conditional log likelihood difference is minus the positively weighted sum of finite-response-space KL divergences. Its unique maximizer is eta0 by injectivity. This establishes a population criterion, not finite-sample MLE existence/uniqueness or consistency without further regularity.

finite_likelihood_counterexample.purpose: Refute a literal equality of finite-data biometric likelihood evidence across subsets even in a correctly calibrated model. This does not assert that the dissertation intended exact finite-sample equality.
finite_likelihood_counterexample.design: Four distinct conditionally independent Rasch observations per twin, all with known slope1 and difficulty0; subsets S={1,2}, U={3,4}. At least one independent MZ family and one independent DZ family are observed at EACH of M=0 and M=1. Subsets use the same fully observed families. This supplies all four joint-support cells required by the conditional population identification argument.
finite_likelihood_counterexample.parameters: At BOTH moderator levels, mu=0 and T=1. Point P: A=1/4,C=1/4,E=1/2. Point Q: A=1/2,C=1/8,E=3/8. All moderator slopes are0; log intercepts are finite. Both points have strictly positive components summing to1. K_DZ=A/2+C=3/8 at BOTH points, while K_MZ=A+C rises from1/2 at P to5/8 at Q. All covariances are interior. Means, total variance, calibration, observation design and moderator support are unchanged.
finite_likelihood_counterexample.realized_full_data: In every MZ family, items1/2 are both1 in both twins, whereas items3/4 are both1 in twin1 and both0 in twin2. DZ families can have ANY fixed binary response vectors, with identical realized data retained for the comparison of P against Q. At least one family is present in each of the four support cells.
exact_derivation: Write f(x)=logistic(x), v(x)=f(x)^2, u(x)=(1-f(x))^2. Both functions and their derivatives are bounded, with vprime>0 and uprime<0 at every finite x.

For an MZ family the S pattern probability is E[v(theta1)v(theta2)] and the U pattern probability is E[v(theta1)u(theta2)]. Holding mu=0,T=1 fixed, their derivatives with respect to interior K are respectively E[vprime(theta1)vprime(theta2)]>0 and E[vprime(theta1)uprime(theta2)]<0. The Gaussian covariance derivative identity and integration by parts apply because of bounded derivatives and Gaussian tails.

Every DZ family has the exact SAME bivariate latent Gaussian distribution at P and Q: same means, variances and covariance3/8. With the same calibrated response kernels, every DZ response-vector probability is therefore identical at P and Q. This remains true after taking either item subset and for arbitrary fixed DZ response data. Positive DZ likelihood factors cancel separately in each P-versus-Q likelihood ratio.

The MZ covariance increases from1/2 to5/8. Multiplying independent positive family probabilities gives L_S(Q)>L_S(P), while L_U(Q)<L_U(P). Hence two admissible subsets give opposite finite likelihood orderings of the same two biometric parameter points, which differ in heritability A/T as well as C/T and E/T.

Every specified full-data pattern, including arbitrary DZ vectors, has strictly positive probability at each interior parameter point: all conditional Bernoulli factors lie strictly between0 and1 and the expectation of their product is positive.

Each two-item subset nevertheless retains two distinct conditionally independent known positive-slope observations, and the design retains both zygosities at both moderator levels. The conditional population identification theorem applies to each subset; it is compatible with these different finite-data likelihood orderings.

exact_arithmetic_check.method: Python standard-library Fraction assertions; no model fitting, simulation or numerical integration

finite_likelihood_counterexample.limits: No optimizer, posterior, simulation or numerical approximation is used. These strict fixed-parameter likelihood comparisons do NOT establish opposite unconstrained global MLEs, posterior summaries or significance decisions; such a stronger claim is unnecessary and is not made.

precision_and_selection: The information about a fixed latent theta from a conditionally independent calibrated subset is sum_j a_j^2*p_j(theta)*(1-p_j(theta)); changing item count, difficulty or discrimination generally changes it. This is conditional measurement information, not a formula for biometric standard errors.

Population-target invariance does not imply identical finite estimates, intervals, power, likelihood ratios, or significance decisions. The exact example supplies a finite-likelihood failure of invariance; the source itself acknowledges poor-tail information on p107.

Response-dependent subset selection, unmodeled informative missingness, changing ascertainment/population, calibration error, conditional dependence or misspecification can break the stated bridge. Such violations are not asserted to have occurred in the source data.

scale_distinction.common_scale: The result compares subsets on one anchored measurement scale, not arbitrary transformations.
scale_distinction.affine_bookkeeping: If theta_star=c*theta+d with c>0 and the known item calibration is transformed coherently, ACE variances multiply by c^2, while heritability remains unchanged. For the stated measured-M log-linear variances, intercepts shift by 2*log(c) and slopes remain unchanged when moderator coding is fixed. Thus even affine changes do not preserve raw variance values.
scale_distinction.nonlinear: A nonlinear latent transformation generally changes the Gaussian/log-linear model family. No invariance to such transformations is established; the source acknowledges arbitrary scale choice on pp107-108.

remaining_gaps: Chapter2 and related latent-genetic interaction models need identification of their non-Gaussian latent response distribution and biometric parameters for each proposed subset. The reviewed conditional Gaussian two-item argument does not supply it. Common IRT scaling alone is not this missing injectivity proof.
The dichotomous logistic proof does not certify every ordinal, polytomous or multidimensional measurement model used elsewhere, nor arbitrary subsets lacking the requisite observable moments.
Actual empirical calibration, local independence, joint support, missingness and correct latent model are not independently verified here; unavailable empirical inputs remain separate blockers.

No faithful Lean formalization/bridge is supplied. This ordinary written analytical check does not clear the formal proved-results manuscript gate and has not yet received a separate independent review.

source_assumptions_read.content: Both MZ and DZ groups (28%/72%); shared binary moderator; known difficulties evenly spread-3.2to3.2; J20/60/100/250. These item counts provide at least two distinct finite difficulties.
Empirical model uses known OPLM item discrimination parameters. The equal-discrimination proof below does not automatically cover unequal discrimination.

theorem.target: Population/global injectivity of the eight biometric/mean coefficients in the observed calibrated Rasch item-vector distribution, restricted to the source simulation model/design assumptions.
required_assumptions: Gaussian latent twin trait at each moderator value with shared mean and variance across zygosity
A(m),C(m),E(m)>0 finite and loglinear in shared moderator
Known MZ/DZ genetic correlations1and1/2; no other covariance components
Both MZ and DZ groups have positive observed support at EACH of the two distinct moderator levels: all four zygosity-by-moderator cells, not merely positive marginal support
At least two known finite distinct difficulties with common fixed Rasch discrimination1; same calibration across groups/moderator

Population item marginals and at least one cross-twin joint item probability identifiable from observations; complete item/pair observation or justified missingness conditions sufficient for those probabilities
Conditional independence of item responses given latent traits, as in the stated Rasch measurement model

proof.name: Mean is identified conditional on latent standard deviation
proof.statement: For a known finite difficulty b1, define p1(mu,s)=E[L(mu+sZ-b1)] with Z standard normal, L logistic and s>0. For fixed s, p1 is continuous strictly increasing in mu, with limits0and1. Thus for any p in(0,1), a unique mu_p(s) exists. Its derivative is mu_p'(s)=-E[Z L'(mu_p(s)+sZ-b1)]/E[L'(mu_p(s)+sZ-b1)].
proof.justification: L'>0 everywhere and is bounded; dominated convergence gives limits and differentiation. E|Z| is finite; the implicit derivative is legitimate since denominator>0.

proof.name: A second distinct calibrated difficulty identifies the standard deviation
proof.statement: Let b2>b1. Define f'(z)=L'(mu_p(s)+sz-b1), g'(z)=L'(mu_p(s)+sz-b2), and probability weight w_s(z) proportional to f'(z)phi(z). Along the p1=p curve, d p2(mu_p(s),s)/ds = E[f'] Cov_w(Z, g'/f'). The ratio is r(t)=d(1+t)^2/(d+t)^2, where t=exp(mu_p(s)+sZ-b1), d=exp(b2-b1)>1. Its derivative wrt t is2d(d-1)(t+1)/(d+t)^3>0. Hence r is strictly increasing in Z when s>0.
proof.strictness: Under w_s the variable Z has a positive density onR. For independent Z,Z', Cov_w(Z,r(Z))=E[(Z-Z')(r(Z)-r(Z'))]/2>0. Therefore p2 is strictly increasing along the fixed-p1 curve. Equal pairs(p1,p2) imply equal s, then equal mu.
proof.limit: The two difficulties must be known, finite and distinct, with the same fixed unit discrimination. This step uses population item probabilities, not observed finite-sample proportions.

proof.name: Cross-twin item probability identifies latent covariance
proof.statement: With identified mu and T=s^2, fix any known item difficulty for each twin. For jointly Gaussian centered(X,Y) of variances T and covariance K with |K|<T, define q(K)=E[L(mu+X-bj)L(mu+Y-bk)]. Then q'(K)=E[L'(mu+X-bj)L'(mu+Y-bk)]>0.
proof.derivation: For the bivariate normal density phi_K, direct differentiation gives partial_K phi_K=partial_x partial_y phi_K. Differentiating the integral and integrating by parts twice moves derivatives to the two logistic factors. Gaussian tails, bounded logistic factors and bounded derivatives make boundary terms vanish and justify the operations on compact subsets of|K|<T. The integrand product of derivatives is strictly positive.
proof.consequence: Population joint response probability for a chosen cross-twin item pair therefore determines K uniquely. This uses one such probability in each zygosity group, after mean and variance are identified.

proof.name: Recover A,C,E at each moderator level
proof.statement: At fixed m, T=A+C+E, K_MZ=A+C, K_DZ=A/2+C. Hence A=2(K_MZ-K_DZ), C=2K_DZ-K_MZ and E=T-K_MZ uniquely.
proof.assumptions: Common latent mean/variance across zygosity groups at the same shared family moderator; known genetic correlations1and1/2; both groups observable at EACH moderator level used for coefficient recovery. PositiveA,C,E imply0<K_DZ<K_MZ<T, within step3 domain.

proof.name: Recover moderator coefficients
proof.statement: At two distinct moderator levels m0,m1, with both MZ and DZ groups observed at EACH level, recovered positive variances V_r determine beta1r=[logV_r(m1)-logV_r(m0)]/(m1-m0) and beta0r=logV_r(m0)-beta1r*m0 for r=A,C,E. The recovered means similarly determine mu and beta1m. Consequently the8-dimensional population parameter vector is injectively mapped to the observed item-vector distributions under the listed design/calibration assumptions.
proof.scope: For binary shared moderator0/1 this is directly constructive. Continuous moderator generalization requires identifiable conditional distributions at enough support points or continuity plus equality almost everywhere; no unsupported extrapolation from missing moderator support.

theorem.conclusion: Two parameter vectors satisfying these assumptions with equal observed distributions have equal mean/variance at each moderator level, equal MZ/DZ covariance, equalA/C/E and equal mean/logvariance coefficients.

constructive_design_failures.reason: The two distinct(A,C,E)triples give exactly the same joint latent Gaussian distribution and therefore every observed item-vector probability. This is a direct equality argument, not parameter counting.
constructive_design_failures.exclusion: The source simulation includes both zygosity groups, so this is a design-necessity example, not its counterexample.

constructive_design_failures.reason: Every variance slope and the mean slope multiply0, so arbitrary distinct finite slopes give the same observed distribution.

constructive_design_failures.exclusion: The source simulation treats difficulties as known.

conditional_statement.measurement: Y1,Y2 are two distinct conditionally independent binary observations given theta; P(Y1=1|theta)=f(theta)=L(a1*theta-d1), P(Y2=1|theta)=g(theta)=L(a2*theta-d2), with known finite d1,d2 and known finite positive slopes. Reorder the two items so0<a2<=a1. If the source writes L(a_j*(theta-b_j)), set d_j=a_j*b_j.
conditional_statement.latent: theta=mu+sZ with Z standard normal, finite mu and s>0.
conditional_statement.observed_target: Population p=E[Y1]=E[f(theta)] and q=E[Y1Y2]=E[f(theta)g(theta)]. The joint equality requires conditional independence; two repeated labels of the same binary draw do not suffice.
conditional_statement.claim: The mapping(mu,s) to(p,q) is globally injective onR times(0,infinity) under these conditions. No difference between d1 and d2 or between slopes is required.

derivation.name: Fixed marginal determines a mean curve
derivation.argument: For every finite s>0,p(mu,s)=E f(mu+sZ) is continuous and strictly increasing in mu because fprime>0. Its limits as mu tends to minus/plus infinity are0/1. Hence every p in(0,1) defines one mu_p(s). The implicit derivative is mu_pprime(s)=-E[Z fprime]/E[fprime]. Differentiation is justified by fprime<=a1/4 and finite E|Z|; positive denominator yields localC1 curves that agree globally by uniqueness.

derivation.name: Derivative of the within-person joint probability
derivation.argument: Let h=fg and w_s(z)=fprime(mu_p(s)+sz)phi(z)/E[fprime]. Differentiating q along the fixed-p curve gives E[Z hprime]-E[hprime]E[Z fprime]/E[fprime] = E[fprime]Cov_w(Z,r(mu_p(s)+sZ)), where r=hprime/fprime.

derivation.name: Positive-slope ordering makes the ratio strictly increasing
derivation.strict_sign: With c=a2/a1 in(0,1],the bracket=(1-c)+2c(1-g)>0 because0<g<1. Also a2>0,0<f<1. Thus rprime(theta)>0 for every finite theta, including equal slopes. Since s>0,r(mu_p(s)+sZ) is strictly increasing inZ.
derivation.symbolic_validation: Independent chain-rule differentiation using fprime=a1*f*(1-f),gprime=a2*g*(1-g) equals the displayed expression exactly. Identical-calibration limit g=f,a2=a1 gives rprime=2*a1*f*(1-f)>0.

derivation.name: Integrability and strict covariance
derivation.argument: For unequal slopes r may be unbounded, so bounded-r reasoning would be invalid. Instead fprime*r=hprime=fprime*g+f*gprime satisfies0<hprime<=(a1+a2)/4. Thus E_w[r]=E[hprime]/E[fprime] and E_w[|Z|r]=E[|Z|hprime]/E[fprime] are finite, as is E_w|Z|. The independent-copy identity Cov_w(Z,r(Z))=E[(Z-Zprime)(r(Z)-r(Zprime))]/2 is therefore valid. Weight w has positive density on allR and r is strictly increasing, making this covariance strictly positive.

derivation.name: Global identification of latent mean and variance
derivation.argument: Consequently q(mu_p(s),s) is strictly increasing over the connected domain s>0. Two parameter vectors with equalp andq must have equals and then equalmu. This is global injectivity, not just a nonsingular Jacobian at one point.

derivation.name: Cross-twin covariance and ACE bridge
derivation.argument: After mean and T=s^2 are identified at a fixed moderator level, a cross-twin item joint probability is strictly increasing in latent covarianceK for|K|<T: its derivative equals E[fjprime(theta1)*fkprime(theta2)]>0. The Gaussian identity partial_Kphi=partial_xpartial_yphi, followed by two justified integrations byparts, is unchanged by known positive unequal slopes since logistic factors and derivatives are bounded. MZ/DZ covariances then yield A=2(KMZ-KDZ),C=2KDZ-KMZ,E=T-KMZ. Two moderator levels recover all logvariance and mean coefficients.
derivation.required_joint_support: Both MZ andDZ groups must have positive observed support at EACH of the two distinct moderator levels. Within-person p/q and cross-twin item probabilities must be identifiable at those levels. Positive marginal support alone is insufficient.
derivation.other_bridge_assumptions: Same finite Gaussian mean/variance across zygosity at each shared moderator level; finite strictlypositive ACE; known genetic correlations1/.5; fixed invariant calibration and conditional measurement independence. The previously reviewed explicit inversion and support limits remain applicable.

model_and_assumptions: Observed zygosity Z has positive probability for MZ and DZ. The shared family moderator M is observed without error; its conditional law nu_z is common when comparing two candidate parameter points, as follows from equality of observed joint laws. Treat its distribution as ancillary or fixed rather than imposing a parameter-dependent unexamined selection model.
For each zygosity, nu_z is not concentrated on any set of at most three real values. MZ and DZ supports may be disjoint; no conditioning on specified zero-probability points is required.

One common finite eight-parameter vector eta defines mu(m)=mu0+mu1*m, A(m)=exp(a0+a1*m), C(m)=exp(c0+c1*m), E(m)=exp(e0+e1*m) for every real m. These positive functions, including the same mean and components across zygosity, are assumed exactly, not empirically demonstrated.

Conditional on M=m,Z=z, twin traits are jointly Gaussian with equal marginal mean mu(m), variance T(m)=A(m)+C(m)+E(m), covariance K_MZ(m)=A(m)+C(m) or K_DZ(m)=A(m)/2+C(m). Known genetic correlations are1 and1/2. The covariances are strictly interior because E>0.

Known finite invariant logistic calibration anchors trait location and scale; at least two distinct conditionally independent binary observations with strictly positive finite slopes are available within a person. Distinct observations may have identical calibration. Cross-twin item joint probabilities are also identified. Conditional independence is across the relevant observations given latent traits.

The full conditional observed item law supplies the within-person marginal/joint and cross-twin joint probabilities for nu_z-almost every m. Complete item observation suffices; with missingness/selection this availability is an additional assumption, not an automatic consequence of marginal item observation or this proof.
continuous-moderator-identification-chec.theorem: Under these assumptions equality of population observed joint distributions of (Z,M,item responses) for eta and eta_prime implies eta=eta_prime. This is global population injectivity, not a statement about sample likelihood shape.

ordinary_proof.name: Conditional-law equality without pointwise support assumptions
ordinary_proof.argument: Equality of joint observed laws implies equal zygosity probabilities and moderator laws and equal conditional item probability vectors nu_z-almost everywhere. The finite binary response space permits one common full-measure equality set S_z. By the support assumption S_z contains at least four distinct real values: otherwise nu_z would be concentrated on at most three values. No claim is made that a regular conditional law is intrinsically fixed at an arbitrary zero-mass point.

ordinary_proof.name: Recover latent moments on those equality sets
ordinary_proof.argument: Apply the independently reviewed joint-item identification lemma at every m in S_z: with known positive slopes, one marginal and one within-person joint probability globally identify finite Gaussian mean mu(m) and positive variance T(m). The cross-twin joint probability then strictly increases in K_z(m) by the Gaussian covariance derivative E[fprime(theta1)gprime(theta2)]>0, so it identifies K_z(m). Bounded logistic derivatives justify the Gaussian differentiation. Thus both candidate parameter points have identical mu,T,K_z on S_z. This step is conditional on the pinned earlier proof and its stated local-independence/calibration assumptions.

ordinary_proof.name: Real exponential zero-count lemma
ordinary_proof.argument: For distinct ordered real lambda_1<...<lambda_r and nonzero real coefficients c_j, a nonzero F(x)=sum_j c_j exp(lambda_j*x) has at most r-1 distinct real zeros. For r=1 there are none. Induct: G=exp(-lambda_1*x)F has exactly the same zeros. If it has r distinct zeros, Rolle gives at least r-1 distinct zeros of Gprime=sum_{j=2}^r c_j(lambda_j-lambda_1)exp((lambda_j-lambda_1)*x). All r-1 coefficients are nonzero and exponents distinct, so induction allows at most r-2 zeros, contradiction. The same argument excludes any larger or infinite zero set by selecting r zeros. Before applying the lemma, group equal exponents and remove zero coefficients; if no terms remain, the function is identically zero.

ordinary_proof.name: Extend both covariance equalities globally
ordinary_proof.argument: For either z, K_z^eta-K_z^eta_prime is a sum of at most four real exponentials: the A and C terms from each candidate, with genetic coefficient1 or1/2. After grouping coincident slopes and cancellations there are r<=4 nonzero terms, or none. Equality on S_z gives at least four distinct zeros. The lemma forces the difference to be identically zero on R. This applies separately to each zygosity, so disjoint supports cause no gap in this exact functional model.

ordinary_proof.name: Invert ACE then the affine coefficients
ordinary_proof.argument: Global equality of both K curves yields A=2(K_MZ-K_DZ) and C=2*K_DZ-K_MZ equal globally. Their logarithms are affine, so equality at any two distinct real values identifies a0,a1,c0,c1. At any two distinct values in S_MZ, T equality and A,C equality give E equality; log E is affine, identifying e0,e1. Likewise mean equality on those two values identifies mu0,mu1. The two-point affine design determinant is m1-m0, nonzero. Thus all eight coefficients agree.

non-gaussian-latent-moment-check.parameter_domain: All calculations condition on one finite fixed parameter vector (mu,va,vc,beta0,beta), with va>0,vc>=0,ve=exp(beta0)>0. Source inverse-gamma priors place va,vc in the strictly positive interior; allowing vc=0 is a harmless extension, not a different prior. No averaging over parameter priors is used.

source_faithful_representation.notation: Source C_i has mean mu. Write centered C=C_i-mu ~N(0,vc); this centered variable is independent of genetic innovations. Let Z1,Z2 be independent standard normals independent of all genetic/common effects.
source_faithful_representation.genetics: For MZ, A1=A2~N(0,va). For DZ, A_t=G+H_t with G,H1,H2 mutually independent N(0,va/2). Thus each A_t~N(0,va) and Cov(A1,A2)=rho*va, rho=1 or1/2. Independence of common effect and Gaussian innovations follows the source conditional hierarchy.
source_faithful_representation.trait: Theta_t=mu+A_t+C+sqrt(ve*exp(beta*A_t))*Z_t. This expresses Eqs2.7–2.8 and2.14–2.15, with ve=exp(beta0), beta=beta1. Within MZ pairs the residual variance factor is shared, but residual draws remain conditionally independent.
source_faithful_representation.conditions: Same fixed parameters across both zygosity populations, known genetic correlations1 and1/2, independent residual innovations and centered common effects as above. Both populations must be available. This is not a Gaussian marginal trait assumption when beta is nonzero.

non-gaussian-latent-moment-check.theorem: The map from this fixed parameter vector to the latent-population moments (mean mu, marginal variance T, MZ covariance K_MZ, DZ covariance K_DZ, marginal third central moment m3) is globally injective on the stated domain. Therefore equality of the two latent twin population distributions implies equality of the parameter vector. Finite Rasch item-response probabilities have not been shown to identify these latent moments.

ordinary_proof.name: Absolute moments exist at fixed finite parameters
ordinary_proof.argument: For any positive integer k, the Gaussian A+C has finite absolute kth moment. Independence of Z and A gives E|sqrt(ve exp(beta A))*Z|^k=ve^(k/2) E exp(k beta A/2) E|Z|^k, finite since the centered Gaussian mgf equals exp(va t^2/2) for every finite real t. The inequality |x+y|^k<=2^(k-1)(|x|^k+|y|^k) proves finite absolute central trait moments. Cross-products are integrable by Cauchy–Schwarz. Thus conditional expectation and the cubic expansion below are legitimate. This does not assert existence of the trait mgf at nonzero arguments.

ordinary_proof.name: Mean and twin covariance
ordinary_proof.argument: Given A1,A2,C, each residual has mean zero, so ETheta_t=mu. Its conditional cross residual product expectation is zero because Z1 and Z2 are independent and centered, including the shared-scale MZ case. Residual–genetic/common cross terms also vanish. Therefore K_MZ=va+vc and K_DZ=va/2+vc. Shared random residual scale may induce higher-order dependence; it does not add second cross covariance.

ordinary_proof.name: Marginal variance
ordinary_proof.argument: Write X=A+C and H=sqrt(ve exp(beta A)). Conditional residual variance is H^2 and conditional mean is mu+X. Total variance gives T=va+vc+ve E exp(beta A)=va+vc+ve exp(beta^2 va/2). Define R=T-va-vc=ve exp(beta^2 va/2)>0. In particular ve is environmental variance at A=0; the population residual contribution is R, which generally differs from ve.

ordinary_proof.name: Third central moment
ordinary_proof.argument: Condition on A,C and use EZ=EZ^3=0,EZ^2=1: E[(Theta-mu)^3|A,C]=(A+C)^3+3(A+C)ve exp(beta A). The centered Gaussian A+C has zero third moment. Since C is independent of A and centered, E[C exp(beta A)]=0. Differentiating the Gaussian mgf yields E[A exp(beta A)]=va beta exp(beta^2 va/2). Differentiation is justified, for example, by completing the square and integrability of |A| exp(tA) uniformly for t in a compact neighborhood of beta. Consequently m3=3 va beta ve exp(beta^2 va/2)=3 va beta R.

ordinary_proof.name: Explicit inverse and global latent identification
ordinary_proof.argument: Recover va=2(K_MZ-K_DZ), vc=2*K_DZ-K_MZ, and R=T-va-vc. Because va,R>0, recover beta=m3/(3 va R), then ve=R exp(-beta^2 va/2)>0 and beta0=log(R)-beta^2 va/2. The mean recovers mu directly. Every step is single valued. Thus equal specified latent moments imply equal parameters; no local Jacobian or parameter-count argument is being substituted for global injectivity.

ordinary_proof.name: Sign and zero-interaction limits
ordinary_proof.argument: Because3 va R>0, m3 and beta have the same sign and m3=0 iff beta=0 within the stated domain. When beta=0 the trait pair is jointly Gaussian, R=ve and m3=0. When beta is nonzero the nonzero finite third central moment proves the marginal trait is not Gaussian. Thus the earlier Gaussian item-identification lemma cannot be applied in that case.

boundaries_and_limits.finding: A=0 almost surely, so exp(beta A)=1 for every beta. Beta is unidentifiable and the inverse divides by zero. Excluded; no claim of stable estimation as va approaches zero.
The interaction disappears; outside the finite beta0 domain. R must be positive.
Formulas remain valid for this fixed-parameter boundary, with genetic/common construction interpreted using degenerate C. Source prior remains strictly positive.

rasch-sufficiency-derivation.source_scope: Schwabe2016 Chapter2pp19-20 andChapter5pp77-78 known item difficulties with Rasch responses; original sumscore comparator instead rescales totals and uses Gaussian phenotype model.
assumptions: Known fixed finite item difficulties b_j
Conditionally independent Bernoulli responses with logit p_j=theta-b_j
All retained observed items and their difficulties/missingness pattern known
Parameters being inferred occur only through latent theta law; item calibration not estimated
proof: For a response vector y with S=sum(y_j), p(y|theta,b)=exp(S*theta-sum(b_j*y_j))/product_j(1+exp(theta-b_j)).
Let c_s(b) be the coefficient of z^s in product_j(1+exp(-b_j)*z). Summing patterns at fixed S=s gives p(S=s|theta,b)=c_s(b)*exp(s*theta)/product_j(1+exp(theta-b_j)).

Their ratio exp(-sum(b_j*y_j))/c_S(b) is constant in theta and every latent-model parameter. For multiple people, multiply these constants, integrate the same correlated latent law and multiply the same priors. The normalized posterior on all latent-model quantities is identical.

Thus exact score-likelihood calculation can preserve the item model, even for non-Gaussian moderated ACE latent laws. This does not justify the dissertation Gaussian/rescaled sumscore comparator and says nothing about its bias.

If item parameters are inferred, the dropped constants depend on them, so retaining only S generally loses calibration information. With different observed-item masks the corresponding b subset and mask must be retained; missingness ignorability is a separate assumption.

notation.likelihood: theta_t | A,C ~ Normal(mu+C+A_t, variance exp(beta0+beta1*A_t)); y_tk | theta_t ~ Bernoulli(logistic(theta_t-b_k)). Preserve actual responses and fixed known item difficulties.

unchanged_priors: Independent ta, tc ~ Gamma(shape=1, rate=1). Thus va and vc have inverse-Gamma(shape=1, scale=1) priors, not flat variance priors.
mu and beta1 ~ Normal(0, variance=10); beta0 ~ Normal(0, variance=1); ve=exp(beta0).
Do not replace these with priors on total variance, variance proportions, or residual precision.

direct_centered_representation.MZ: A_i ~ Normal(0, va); define A_i1=A_i2=A_i deterministically. Keep two distinct theta values and both response vectors.
direct_centered_representation.DZ: A_i1 ~ Normal(0, va); A_i2 | A_i1 ~ Normal(rho*A_i1, va*(1-rho^2)), with rho=1/2. The second conditional precision is ta/(1-rho^2)=4*ta/3.
direct_centered_representation.singularity: Never use the DZ conditional with rho=1: its variance becomes zero. Declare MZ and DZ genetic coordinates separately. MZ genetic dimension is one, not two.
direct_centered_representation.monitors: Reassemble the original family order and all a[i,t], c[i], theta[i,t], and p[i,t,k] nodes. Preserve the same fourteen monitored columns, including selected family-1 MZ nodes and derived log variances.

joint_target_equivalence.baseline_map: C=sqrt(vc)*zc; MZ A=sqrt(va)*za; DZ A1=sqrt(va)*za and A2=sqrt(va)*(rho*za+sqrt(1-rho^2)*zb). Active z coordinates are independent standard normals.
joint_target_equivalence.forward_Jacobian: J = vc^(N/2) * va^(n_MZ/2+n_DZ) * (1-rho^2)^(n_DZ/2). This is the absolute determinant for active z -> (C,A) coordinates. Including unchanged global parameters makes the full transform block triangular, so parameter dependence adds no further determinant.
joint_target_equivalence.density_identity: p_centered(C,A,globals,theta,y) = p_noncentered(z(C,A,globals),globals,theta,y) / J. The normal densities and 1/J give exactly the centered C, MZ A, and DZ bivariate normal densities. The substituted theta/item likelihood is identical. The joint target for mapped scientific variables is therefore unchanged.
joint_target_equivalence.unused_MZ_auxiliary: The baseline also declares an unused standard-normal zb for MZ families because its coefficient is zero. Retain it as an independent auxiliary for an augmented-space bijection, or integrate it out. Removing it is marginalization, not an invertible two-to-one dimensional transformation.
joint_target_equivalence.variance_prior_warning: If va rather than ta is declared stochastic, the Jacobian |dta/dva|=va^-2 is necessary; likewise for vc. Retaining the original Gamma precision priors avoids this accidental prior change.

full_conditionals.direct_ta: ta | A,rest ~ Gamma(1+(n_MZ+2*n_DZ)/2, 1+0.5*(sum_MZ A_i^2 + sum_DZ A_i^T R^-1 A_i)), where R^-1=[[1,-rho],[-rho,1]]/(1-rho^2). For 140 MZ and 360 DZ families the shape is 431.
full_conditionals.direct_tc: tc | C,rest ~ Gamma(1+N/2, 1+0.5*sum_i C_i^2). For N=500 the shape is 251.
full_conditionals.reason: Conditional on centered A and C, the theta likelihood no longer depends directly on ta or tc. Their remaining factors are Gaussian latent densities and Gamma priors. In the current noncentered representation, A and C depend on ta/tc inside the likelihood.
full_conditionals.limits: These identities establish conditional conjugacy, not automatic JAGS sampler selection or improved mixing. beta0 and beta1 still enter residual variance exponentially. ve does not gain a Gamma conditional under its unchanged lognormal prior.
